question_text: Explain how bats can ascertain distances, directions, nature, and sizes of the obstacles without any 'eyes'.
answer_text: Bats emit very high-frequency ultrasonic sound waves. These waves get reflected back toward them by obstacles. A bat receives a reflected wave (frequency) and estimates the distance, direction, nature, and size of an obstacle with the help of its brain senses.
final_answer: Thus, bats use echolocation to navigate and identify their surroundings.

question_text: Explain why a violin note and sitar note may have the same frequency, yet we can distinguish between the two notes.
answer_text: The overtones produced by a sitar and a violin, and the strengths of these overtones, are different. Hence, one can distinguish between the notes produced by a sitar and a violin even if they have the same frequency of vibration.
final_answer: Thus, timbre allows us to differentiate between musical instruments.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of sound quality and overtones.

subject: Physics
question_text: Explain why solids can support both longitudinal and transverse waves, but only longitudinal waves can propagate in gases.
answer_text: Solids have shear modulus. They can sustain shearing stress. Since fluids do not have any definite shape, they yield to shearing stress. The propagation of a transverse wave is such that it produces shearing stress in a medium. The propagation of such a wave is possible only in solids, and not in gases. Both solids and fluids have their respective bulk moduli. They can sustain compressive stress. Hence, longitudinal waves can propagate through solids and fluids.
final_answer: Therefore, the ability to support different types of waves depends on the medium's properties.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of wave propagation in different media.

question_text: A train, standing at the outer signal of a railway station blows a whistle of frequency 400 Hz in still air. (i) What is the frequency of the whistle for a platform observer when the train (a) approaches the platform with a speed of 10 m/s, (b) recedes from the platform with a speed of 10 m/s? (ii) What is the speed of sound in each case? The speed of sound in still air can be taken as 340 m/s.

mcq_options.option_text: approaches the platform with a speed of 10 m/s,
recedes from the platform with a speed of 10 m/s? (ii) What is the speed of sound in each case? The speed of sound in still air can be taken as 340 m/s.

parts.part_text: What is the frequency of the whistle for a platform observer when the train approaches the platform with a speed of 10 m/s?
parts.answer_text: The apparent frequency of the whistle as the train approaches the platform is given by the relation: \( f' = f \left( \frac{v + v_o}{v - v_s} \right) \). Substituting the values, we get \( f' = 400 \left( \frac{340 + 0}{340 - 10} \right) = 412.12 \text{ Hz} \).

steps.description: Identify the formula for apparent frequency when the source approaches the observer.
Substitute the values into the formula.
Calculate the apparent frequency.

parts.final_answer: Thus, the frequency of the whistle for the observer when the train approaches is 412.12 Hz.

parts.part_text: What is the frequency of the whistle for a platform observer when the train recedes from the platform with a speed of 10 m/s?
parts.answer_text: The apparent frequency of the whistle as the train recedes from the platform is given by the relation: \( f' = f \left( \frac{v - v_o}{v + v_s} \right) \). Substituting the values, we get \( f' = 400 \left( \frac{340 - 0}{340 + 10} \right) = 388.57 \text{ Hz} \).

steps.description: Identify the formula for apparent frequency when the source recedes from the observer.
Substitute the values into the formula.
Calculate the apparent frequency.

parts.final_answer: Thus, the frequency of the whistle for the observer when the train recedes is 388.57 Hz.

difficulty_reasoning: Involves application of the Doppler effect and calculations.
